text:
sanjay: Heads up — we put merge 0427 (proto v2 fragmentation + toolcall refactor) out to canary and CI is showing an ~18% increase in p95 for streaming SSE endpoints. Holding the rollout.

maya: Where is the regression showing up? runtime, proxy, or infra?

sanjay: Runtime stack. Quick profiler shows hot in serialization/toolcall handshake. KV hit rate looks steady but effective batch sizes dropped ~30% on the affected traces.

olivia: Can you paste the flamegraph/top stacks you grabbed?

sanjay: Sure — top of sample trace (condensed):
```
serialization::serialize_frame
proto::fragment_writer::flush_chunk
toolcall::handshake::encode_request
net::socket::writev (many small writes)
runtime::kernel_planner::select_kernels
```

henry: I started a bisect locally. PRs in candidate set: #1204 (batching hysteresis/kernel planner tweaks) and #1219 (proto v2 fragmentation + toolcall refactor). #1219 added extra per-chunk framing and an extra memcpy for toolcall metadata.

maya: That extra memcpy + smaller chunk sizes could explain syscall churn. We also changed the SSE flush-window semantics in the proxy in that release which could force more frequent flushes.

sanjay: I grabbed a tcpdump + trace from a slow request; you can see burst of small frames and frequent Nagle-disabled writes that align with the serialization flushes: 
```
[trace] send 512b chunk
send 128b metadata
send 64b toolcall chunk
--- turnaround ---
repeat
```

ci-bot: CI perf job streaming-p95: baseline 210ms -> 247ms (+17.6%) — job streaming-p95/2026-03-18 failed threshold.

olivia: KV metrics? evictions, prefetch latency?

sanjay: Eviction counters stable. However kv-prefetch latency spikes when a chunk boundary triggers an immediate serialize+flush path instead of coalesced write. So caching isn't the root cause, it's fragmentation + serialization overhead.

henry: Plan: bisect exact offending commit between #1204 and #1219. If #1219 reproduces the spike, revert that and re-evaluate batching heuristics afterwards. Starting automated bisect now. @maya can you prepare a revert PR for the proto fragmentation change so we can land quickly if bisect confirms?

maya: On it — I'll draft revert/1219-revert and flag rollout hold. Also adding a canary-only test that simulates small-chunk toolcalls to CI.

sanjay: I'll add a perf unit test that asserts coalesced writes for bursty toolcall patterns and a microbenchmark for serialization memcpy counts.

opsbot: Scheduled rollback window: 20:45 UTC if bisect confirms.

henry: Update: bisect step 3 shows the perf delta reproduces when patch from #1219 is applied. I’ll rerun with build-time flags to isolate the framing vs memcpy parts.

maya: Revert PR opened: #1227 (revert proto fragmentation from #1219) — marking rollout hold in the console and pausing canary.

olivia: Thanks. Once revert lands, let's run the full streaming-p95 CI job and confirm baseline restored before unholding. Also follow up with a plan to: (1) reduce per-chunk memcpy, (2) add coalescing in the proxy, (3) tighten CI gate for small-chunk latencies.

sanjay: Agreed. I'll own the serialization perf follow-up. Henry — can you take the coalescing work?

henry: Yup. Will sync later today. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI run queued for revert PR #1227. streaming-p95 job will re-run; expect ~30m.

opsbot: Rollout hold remains until CI baseline validated.
